findings.title: Variable detection strips only the unspaced {{RAW}}/{{END_RAW}} spelling, so the f1 fix misses tag forms the lexer accepts and the living doc documents

serves.scenario: The lexer opens a block on any tag whose trimmed content is RAW and closes it on /\{\{[ \t]*END_RAW[ \t]*\}\}/, and the living doc tells users the closing tag may be written {{ END_RAW }}. extractAllVariables removes only the exact text {{RAW}}...{{END_RAW}}. A node template such as '{{RAW}}${{name}}{{ END_RAW }}' or '{{ RAW }}${{name}}{{END_RAW}}' renders literally in the lexer, but detection still reports 'name'; with Strict Mode on (the default) and no mapping the node raises a missing-variable error, so the template still cannot carry tag-like text in the node. A lesser side effect of the same text-level regex: a literal {{RAW}} inside a comment, followed later by a real block, makes detection drop every variable in between, so Strict Mode would stop flagging them.

findings.title: Variable detection strips RAW blocks at text level, so a {{RAW}} spelling inside a comment or a variable tag named RAW hides real variables from Strict Mode

serves.scenario: In the n8n node, the strip regex in extractAllVariables is not aware of comments or of the '${{' variable prefix, unlike the lexer. For '{{# wrap samples in {{RAW}} #}} ${{b}} {{RAW}}x{{END_RAW}}' the lexer renders b as a variable, but detection removes everything from the '{{RAW}}' inside the comment to the real END_RAW, so b is never detected and Strict Mode does not flag it when unmapped. The same happens for a variable literally named RAW followed later by a real block: '${{RAW}} ${{b}} {{RAW}}x{{END_RAW}}' detects neither RAW nor b. The failure is silent under-detection (an empty string instead of a missing-variable error), never a wrong render, and the triggers are uncommon.

findings.rubric: The raw scan does not alter templates without RAW (applied to the node's detection path); project goal: correct for the n8n node
findings.reproduction: Call extractAllVariables('{{# use {{RAW}} #}} ${{b}} {{RAW}}x{{END_RAW}}'): expected ['b'], the regex at utils.ts:18 yields []. Call extractAllVariables('${{RAW}} ${{b}} {{RAW}}x{{END_RAW}}'): expected ['RAW','b'], yields []. This is the 'lesser side effect' already named in f5 and left unaddressed by its fix, plus the '${{RAW}}' variant; noted for the lead (for example as an addition to follow-up 0008), not a fix request. A possible narrow change is to strip comments before stripping RAW blocks and to add a '(?<!\$)' lookbehind on the opening tag.
